craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of standing; vyabhicāri utsāha at all-instruments-at-once. Sanskrit-first: idantāvat (THISNESS-FORM per UNC — kept; -ness nominalizes); akrama (SEQUENCELESS — kept; melts time). Rows: 9 (mind/speech/senses/pots — all instruments drummed), 1 (‘unceasing’ closes — duration last). Close: ‘at once, unceasing’. Rupture: comma (thisness stated, then its force — form, then melting). Rejected: ‘this’ for thisness — killed: -ness nominalizes; ‘instantly’ for at-once — killed: sakṛt kept at-once. Read aloud: JUST-this-NESS — YOUR-form, POW-er-JUICED; WHERE-se-quence-FAILS … MAY-i-STAND that-FORM at-ONCE, un-CEAS-ing.

lines: Just thisness — Your form, power-juiced; where sequence fails,
time-reckoning melts by force. By mind, speech, senses, pots — may I stand that form at once, unceasing.
l4.sanskrit_cite: idantāvad rūpaṃ tava bhagavataḥ śaktisarasaṃ | tadrūpaṃ yugapad adhitiṣṭheyam aniśam
